name: @olai/plugin-api
//name: IT WAS `@olai/plugins`, in `packages/plugins/`, and the rename is what made room for the tenants. It then held two things at once — the INTERFACE a plugin is written against, and the REGISTRY that names every plugin — and the second half left for `@olai/bundle` when the first became something a plugin IMPORTS. What is here now is the interface and nothing else: the services a plugin names, the events it listens on, and the shapes it hands over. It imports no plugin, which is the whole of why a plugin may import it.
//exports: TWO DOORS, and the split is about which PROCESS opens them rather than about which package does. The ROOT is what a BROWSER half is written against — the six SLOTS a face may hang in and the five service TAGS a half names in its `needs` (src/browser.ts), the face TYPES that say what each of those faces is handed and what it answers with, `JSX.Element` throughout (src/plugin.ts) — plus `definePlugin`, and the shapes both halves share. It used to be the DRESSINGS, the chrome slots and the marks: hooks on an `OlaiPlugin` manifest object a compiled-in registry walked. The object is a plugin now — an Effect whose registrations are finalizers on its own scope — so what it used to DECLARE it REGISTERS, and this door carries the table it registers into rather than the fields it declared. `./services` is what a SERVER half is written against: the service TAGS a plugin lists in its `needs`, the one waterfall it may add a link to, and `definePlugin` beside them. Neither door names `cordis` — the plugin runtime is `@olai/effect-cordis`, which this package imports and nobody else does. Neither door reaches a plugin either, so the graph claims the fence used to make about this package are now claims about `@olai/bundle`; what is left here for the fence to hold is that the SERVICES door pulls no `solid-js`, which is the same hazard one door over — a server that reached a browser face through the interface would evaluate a `.tsx` and die on `react/jsx-dev-runtime` before it served anything.
//: WHAT A PLUGIN IS WRITTEN AGAINST — src/plugin.ts argues the browser half, src/contract.ts the shapes both halves share, and src/services.ts the runtime a server half installs itself into. The registry that names the plugins is `@olai/bundle`.
//dependencies: `effect` is what a plugin is WRITTEN IN — an `apply` is an Effect, a registration is a finalizer on a scope, and the schemas a contributed member is declared in are Effect's too. `@olai/acp` is the floor under this package and under `olai-plugin-chat` both, and it is there for ONE tag: an engine plugin registers a `Leg`, an `Adapter` probe and an install sentence, and the shape of that had to live somewhere neither the plugin nor the chat could be forbidden — which is the protocol package, since an engine IS an ACP agent and how to reach one. Type-only from here, so no SDK code and no zod enter this closure. `@olai/effect-cordis` is the plugin RUNTIME, translated: this package holds olai's tags and event names and imports the bridge, and the bridge is the one package in the tree that names `cordis`. That arrow runs one way and only this far — `packages/bundle/src/fence.test.ts` refuses `cordis` in every other package, including this one. `solid-js` is TYPES ONLY — `JSX.Element` is the return of every face a dressing or a chrome slot names, and a type import puts no runtime on any graph. NO plugin, which is the direction that lets a plugin import this package at all. NO `@olai/surface`, deliberately and structurally: surface depends on THIS package, so a dependency back would be the cycle the whole arrangement is shaped to make unrepresentable. NO `@olai/format` for the same reason one floor over — the kind table travels as DATA, handed down by the server, and a floor package that imported the vocabulary would be the format learning what a terminal is.
